title: Finite-cover augmentation for unbounded complexes with injective terms
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $r\geq0$, and $U:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to X_{\mathrm{open}}$ a family with $\bigcup_iU_i=X$. Let $I$ be an arbitrary integer-indexed cochain complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] whose terms are injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. The actual section-to-total augmentation $\Gamma(X,I)\to T_U(I)$ of [def-sc-alternating-cech-total-complex] is a quasi-isomorphism. No boundedness or K-injectivity assumption is made.

source.place: Tag 08C1, proof: first paragraph using Tags 01EP and 01FM; parent Steps 1--2

proof.text: For each integer degree, use injective module Cech acyclicity and the ordered-to-increasing comparison to obtain exact positive alternating row cohomology. In degree zero, the sheaf gluing axiom says that restrictions of global sections identify with the kernel; injectivity follows from separatedness. Forgetting global-ring scalars detects exactness. The comparison restricts to the actual increasing tuples and preserves the degree-zero augmentation.

The cone is the total of these augmented exact rows, with the usual cone shift and signs. There are only columns -1 through r-1 because increasing (p+1)-tuples in Fin r are empty for p>=r. For a total cocycle, lift its highest Cech component horizontally, subtract the total boundary, and repeat toward smaller Cech degree. The vertical part changes only the preceding column. At column -1 augmentation injectivity forces the remainder to vanish. The finite number of columns makes this chase terminate with no vertical bound. For r=0 the covering scheme is empty; all section modules vanish. Hence the cone is acyclic and the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism.
